review.note: Drafted by the assistant in M44b under the owner's dated exception, from the sources named and not from a reading of them; the argument is the thing to check, not only the dates.

explanation: The company of 1976 is made out of what the nationalisations took. This atlas puts the wave in March 1975, the banks first and insurance the next day. The banks held much of Portuguese industry, so the electricity concerns followed them into public ownership over that year. EDP is the state deciding what to do with them. The edge claims that the expropriation is a condition of the merger. It does not claim that the expropriation required it. A state can own fourteen companies and leave them fourteen. A government of 1976 chose one company for the whole industry, and the Council of the Revolution of 1975 did not. This run could not point at the decree that set the company up in a source it had read, so the record does not cite it.
